text:
Garry Kasparov was born Garik Kimovich Weinstein in Baku, Azerbaijan SSR, and adopted the surname Kasparov at age twelve. He began serious chess study at age seven and trained at Mikhail Botvinnik's school. Kasparov quickly advanced, winning the Soviet Junior Championship twice before gaining international recognition. He became a Grandmaster in 1980 and achieved the world No. 1 ranking in January 1984, making him the youngest-ever world No. 1.
Kasparov won the World Chess Championship against Anatoly Karpov in 1985, and successfully defended his title in subsequent matches, including a 1986 rematch and a 1987 match. He maintained the top ranking for an extended period, leading the rating list from 1985 until his retirement from regular competitive chess in 2005. Following his retirement, he became politically active, organizing the United Civil Front and opposing the Putin administration, eventually fleeing Russia in 2013.
